kobeissi-productivity-rises-labor-share-:
U.S. nonfarm productivity rose in the second quarter, but the headline number hides a change in distribution. Companies produced more output in the same amount of time, which can be read as an early sign that investment in artificial intelligence and automation is beginning to pay. A rise in productivity, however, does not automatically mean that workers received more.

@@REF@@U.S. productivity rises faster than expected in second quarter (Reuters, 2026-08-06)|https://www.reuters.com/business/us-productivity-rises-faster-than-expected-second-quarter-2026-08-06/|https://www.reuters.com

The Bureau of Labor Statistics preliminary release recorded a 1.4% annualized rise in nonfarm productivity, with output up 1.7% and hours worked up 0.3%. Unit labor costs rose 1.3%, so the productivity gain partly offset the increase in compensation costs. Reuters reported that economists had expected productivity to rise 0.6% and unit labor costs to rise 2.1%. Efficiency was better than expected, while the cost of producing one unit of output rose less than expected.

@@REF@@Productivity and Costs, Second Quarter 2026 Preliminary (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2026-08-06)|https://www.bls.gov/news.release/prod2.nr0.htm|https://www.bls.gov

The original post also needs a small correction. It says inflation-adjusted compensation fell 3.2%, while the BLS table gives a 3.1% decline. The difference is small, yet a primary release has to control the number when the number carries the argument.

The larger signal is labor's share. The BLS says compensation accounted for 52.9% of nonfarm output, the lowest reading in a series that begins in 1947. Productivity gains therefore arrived alongside a smaller share of output going to workers. The rule that creates more output and the rule that divides that output are moving in different directions.

@@CMP@@The business reading|More output per hour and lower unit-cost pressure point to a productivity boom.|The labor-income reading|The share of output accruing to workers reached the lowest point in the recorded series.

This cannot be settled by asking only whether AI raised productivity. Automation may reduce the labor time needed for each unit, while pricing power, profit margins and weaker wage bargaining determine where the extra output ends up. The BLS release shows the distribution result, but it does not prove one single cause. Reuters' references to automation and AI should be read as a possible background, not as a demonstrated causal estimate.

The calendar matters too. These are preliminary figures, and the revised release is scheduled for September 3, 2026. If productivity holds while labor's share rebounds, temporary price or compensation effects will explain more of the gap. If both measures stay in the same direction, the stronger reading is that the channel carrying productivity gains into wages has weakened.
semianalysis-gemini-gcp-tpu-financializa:
Sundar Pichai announced a new operating structure for DeepMind: Demis Hassabis will focus on long-term frontier AI and scientific research, while Koray Kavukcuoglu will lead Gemini engineering, the app, and developer services.

@@REF@@Hassabis becomes Chair of DeepMind and Chief Scientist of Alphabet, while Kavukcuoglu takes day-to-day leadership and Gemini product delivery|https://blog.google/company-news/inside-google/message-ceo/next-chapter-ai-momentum/|https://storage.googleapis.com/gweb-uniblog-publish-prod/images/super-g_1.width-1300.jpg

To understand why that matters, it helps to start with how Google ended up with its current AI organization.

## Two research teams inside Google

DeepMind was founded in Britain in 2010. Google acquired it in 2014, but the lab continued to operate from London with its own research culture.

Google also had a separate internal AI research team. DeepMind began as an outside company that Google bought; the other research team was built inside Google.

Different origins and leaders kept the two groups separate even after they belonged to the same company.

The arrival of ChatGPT in late 2022 changed the pressure on Google. Publishing research was no longer enough; new AI had to become a product and reach users quickly.

Google combined the teams into Google DeepMind in 2023. The goal was to put researchers and computing resources in one organization so decisions and product work could move faster.

@@TIME@@2010|DeepMind founded in Britain|2014|Google acquires DeepMind|2023|DeepMind and Google's internal AI team combine|2026-08-05|Long-term research and product operations get separate leaders@@Three years after combining two research groups, Google divided responsibilities inside the merged organization.@@Google DeepMind · Google · Reuters

## Research and products under one roof

After the merger, DeepMind's job became much larger. It had to research new AI, build Gemini, and help put the system into Search, mobile apps, and business products.

Gemini is the AI program that understands a request and produces an answer. Turning it into a service also requires apps, bug fixes, and enough servers to respond quickly when many people use it.

Coordination with Google Cloud became central. Google Cloud is the business where companies pay to use Google's servers and AI, so one leader was overseeing both long-term research and products that had to ship now.

## Why Google split the roles

Google did not disclose a specific trigger for the change. At the time, however, a major new Gemini model was running behind its planned release and several people who had led Gemini development were leaving.

@@REF@@Reuters reported that the delayed model launch and senior departures formed the backdrop to Hassabis taking long-term research while Kavukcuoglu assumed daily operations and commercialization|https://www.reuters.com/business/google-shakes-up-ai-leadership-deepmind-chief-shifts-role-2026-08-05/

Hassabis will serve as Chair of DeepMind and Chief Scientist of Alphabet. He will concentrate on broad, human-level AI and scientific work while continuing to run the AI drug-discovery company he leads.

Kavukcuoglu will run DeepMind day to day. Model engineering, the Gemini app, and developer products will sit under his operational leadership.

Hassabis is not leaving DeepMind. He will set the long-range research direction, while Kavukcuoglu is responsible for turning research into Gemini and Google Cloud products.

## More than a people reshuffle

AI development needs researchers, specialized chips, servers, and data centers. The industry calls the processing capacity supplied by that equipment compute.

That capacity is limited. Servers assigned to long-term experiments cannot simultaneously serve a Gemini launch or an outside customer.

SemiAnalysis turns this constraint into an investment question. Selling Google's own TPU AI chips to outside labs such as Anthropic can increase Google Cloud revenue, but it can also reduce the spare capacity available to Gemini.

SemiAnalysis estimates that more than 20% of TPU shipments from the third quarter of 2026 through the fourth quarter of 2027 will be sold directly to Anthropic. It also models more than $73 billion of annualized third-party AI infrastructure revenue in 2027, but that is an analyst estimate, not Alphabet guidance.

## Is the spending producing results?

Alphabet spent $44.9 billion on servers, data centers, and other capital projects in the second quarter of 2026. Cash left after operating the business and making those investments was negative $5.9 billion.

In the same quarter, Google Cloud revenue reached $24.8 billion, up 82% from a year earlier, and operating income reached $8.8 billion. The investment bill and the Google Cloud payoff are rising together.

@@CHK@@Servers and data centers|$44.9B|Free cash flow|-$5.9B|Google Cloud revenue|$24.8B|Year-over-year growth|82%|Google Cloud operating income|$8.8B|Google Cloud backlog|$514B@@Alphabet's second quarter shows both the cost of AI infrastructure and the growth it is producing in Google Cloud.@@2026-07-22 · Alphabet 2026 Q2 earnings

The reorganization will succeed if Kavukcuoglu can speed up Gemini releases and turn the larger server bill into Google Cloud revenue and profit.

If Gemini ships on schedule while Google Cloud revenue and profit continue to grow, the split will look productive. If investment keeps rising while launches keep slipping, changing the reporting lines will not have solved the problem.

The central issue is not the DeepMind organization chart itself. It is how Google divides people, budgets, and AI servers between long-term research and products that must earn money now.

The effects should appear over time in Gemini release speed, Google Cloud revenue and profit, and the cash left after building more servers and data centers.

As the bottleneck in AI data centers shifts from the GPUs themselves to the optical links between chips, private startup Lumilens has suddenly entered the market's field of view. Serenity's latest post says the company raised $700 million at a $5.5 billion valuation and has begun shipping equipment under a multiyear, multibillion-dollar agreement with a major hyperscaler. That sounds like another AI infrastructure financing headline. The investable connection is the supply chain underneath Lumilens.

## The supply chain behind a stealth startup

Lumilens describes optical interconnects as the way to move data between AI processors with less distance and power pressure than traditional copper links. Its public materials cover silicon photonics, optical engines, near-package optics, and co-packaged optics. The company is trying to address both scale-out links between servers and scale-up links inside an AI system.

@@REF@@Lumilens official site (Lumilens, 2026-08-07)|https://lumilens.com/
That positioning matters because the company is not presenting a single component in isolation. It is trying to become part of the architecture that hyperscalers choose for their next generation of AI clusters. The website is a company description, not proof of commercial revenue.

## What the $50 million order says

The clearest public supply-chain evidence comes from POET.

@@BAR@@POET initial order|$50 million|Five-year potential purchases|More than $500 million@@The initial POET order is not guaranteed revenue. It is the first stage of a development and supply relationship that depends on qualification. It still matters because Lumilens has committed to a listed optical-engine supplier rather than remaining only a concept company.

@@REF@@POET and Lumilens wafer-level photonic integration agreement (GlobeNewswire, 2026-05-14)|https://www.globenewswire.com/de/news-release/2026/5/14/3294762/0/en/poet-technologies-and-lumilens-advance-wafer-level-photonic-integration-for-next-generation-ai-optical-networks.html|https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/c90ecc6e-9475-47bb-9baa-b92e4d296625
POET's announcement expects engineering samples in late 2026 and a production ramp aligned with hyperscaler deployments in 2027. It also makes the condition explicit: development, qualification, and manufacturing scale must all succeed before the purchase orders become revenue.

## Revenue arrives later than valuation

Lumilens's $5.5 billion valuation and POET's $50 million order are not the same kind of number. The first is a financing price that reflects expectations for a large future market. The second is the starting point of a conditional development and supply relationship. Even if optical interconnect demand grows, the design still has to be adopted, samples must pass customer qualification, and the factory must reach usable yield.

That is why this card is watch rather than a confirmed bullish call. If production ramps with 2027 customer deployments, Lumilens will have converted an AI data-center bottleneck into a contracted supply position. If qualification or manufacturing expansion slips, the large valuation and long supply framework will still be expectations rather than reported results. The dividing line is whether the three stages continue on schedule: product development, customer approval, and manufacturing scale.

bessent-wages-25th-percentile-lead:
Bottom line: Bessent's wage arithmetic is correct. The report does not prove that Trump administration policy caused the improvement.

On August 6, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent rejected the claim that the US economy was improving only for high earners while lower-income households fell behind.

That pattern is called a K-shaped economy. It means one group improves during a recovery while another falls behind and the gap widens.

Bessent cited the Bureau of Labor Statistics report on weekly earnings for Q2 2026. BLS is the federal agency that produces official US jobs, inflation, and wage data.

## What does the chart show?

The lower-pay cutoff rose fastest.

The chart ranks workers by weekly pay and compares three positions. A percentile is a position in that ranked line.

The 25th percentile separates the lowest-paid worker in every four from everyone above that line. The median is the exact middle, and the 75th percentile is where the top quarter begins.

@@BAR@@Bottom-quarter cutoff (25th percentile)|5.5%|5.5|Middle worker (median)|4.6%|4.6|Top-quarter cutoff (75th percentile)|1.5%|1.5@@The lower-pay cutoff rose fastest. Its pace was about 3.7 times the upper-pay cutoff's pace.@@Chart attached to Bessent's X post · BLS Q2 2026 Table 5@@ANIMATE

The dollar figures show the same pattern. The lower cutoff moved from $806 to $850, the middle from $1,196 to $1,251, and the upper cutoff from $1,887 to $1,915.

Bessent's calculation is therefore correct. The 2025 comparison report remains in the source list below.

@@REF@@US weekly earnings, second quarter of 2026 (Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2026-07-21)|https://www.bls.gov/news.release/wkyeng.htm|https://www.bls.gov/images/bls_emblem_2016.png

## What $850 means

The $850 figure is one cutoff between two parts of the wage distribution, not an average for lower-paid workers.

It also does not mean the same group of lower-paid workers received an average 5.5% raise.

## This does not track the same people

The table cannot establish that. BLS takes one picture of the workforce in 2025 and another in 2026.

The person at the cutoff need not be the same in both pictures.

For example, the cutoff can rise if fewer young and relatively low-paid workers are in the sample even when individual pay changes little. This is a composition change: a change caused by comparing a different mix of people.

The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's Wage Growth Tracker instead matches the same person's hourly wage 12 months apart. In June 2026, the middle growth rate was 3.6% overall, 3.4% for job stayers, and 4.1% for job switchers.

The measures do not conflict. BLS tracks a cutoff in the wage ranking, while the Atlanta Fed tracks pay changes for matched people.

@@REF@@Same-person wage changes (Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, 2026-07-09)|https://www.atlantafed.org/research-and-data/data/wage-growth-tracker|https://www.atlantafed.org/-/media/Project/Atlanta/FRBA/Images/chcs/wage-growth-tracker/specific/01/hero.webp

## The gain left after inflation

The middle worker's purchasing power rose about 0.5%.

Nominal pay is the dollar amount on a paycheck. Real pay removes inflation to show how much a worker can actually buy.

The middle worker's nominal weekly pay rose $55 while the Consumer Price Index rose 3.9%. CPI measures changes in the prices households pay for goods and services.

Inflation-adjusted weekly pay moved from $372 to $374, a $2 gain. Most of the increase on the paycheck was therefore absorbed by higher prices.

## Workers included in the report

No. It covers 120.945 million wage and salary workers who usually work at least 35 hours a week.

It excludes the self-employed and part-time workers. In the same report, middle weekly pay for part-time workers fell from $396 to $391.

The result should not be applied to every US worker.

## Why the report cannot prove a policy effect

Not yet. The table shows what changed, not why it changed.

It cannot separate tax policy, hiring demand, industry mix, job switching, and labor supply.

Housing costs, wealth, debt, and people without jobs are also outside the table. One wage report is too narrow to declare the K-shaped economy over.

## Three checks for the next report

Three results should be read together on October 21.

Does the lower-pay cutoff again rise fastest?

Does inflation-adjusted middle weekly pay move above $374?

Does part-time pay rebound?

If all three improve, the policy-success case gets stronger. If only one improves, this quarter is more likely a temporary change than a durable trend.

Aeva, a maker of automotive lidar, has jumped into optical connectivity for AI data centers. Its stock rose 18.3% after hours on news that it signed a joint development agreement (JDA) with an optical engine provider to build a module for deployment at an unnamed major hyperscaler.

## What the deal actually is

Aeva's new Optical Connectivity division is built on porting its existing high-power light sources and silicon photonics technology to data-center use. It's pursuing two tracks: an External Laser Small Form Factor Pluggable (ELSFP) light source and an on-chip integrated light source, targeting initial deployment in the second half of 2027 and a production ramp in 2028. @@REF@@Aeva Launches Optical Connectivity Business, Signs First Customer Agreement for a Major Hyperscaler (Business Wire, 2026-08-05)|https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260805815782/en/Aeva-Launches-Optical-Connectivity-Business-Signs-First-Customer-Agreement-for-a-Major-Hyperscaler

## A $6.1 million company entering a giant's market

Aeva's second-quarter 2026 revenue was $6.1 million, up 11% year over year. But the composition tells a different story: product revenue actually fell from $4.2 million to $2.5 million, while the growth came from services revenue, which jumped from $1.3 million to $3.6 million. The optics market Aeva is now entering already has US players like Coherent and Lumentum and China's Innolight established, and their quarterly revenues run an order of magnitude above Aeva's.

@@REF@@Aeva Q2 Results: $6.1M Revenue, CFO Transition (StockTitan, 2026-08-05)|https://www.stocktitan.net/news/AEVA/aeva-reports-second-quarter-2026-o2lqira9f08h.html|https://static.stocktitan.net/company-logo/aeva-lg.png?v=fa1e3d818f

## A CFO exit and a 2027 deadline

Around the same time as this announcement, Aeva also disclosed that its CFO of six years will leave the company on September 5. There's no evidence the two events are connected, but a finance-chief transition just as a brand-new business unit launches is worth tracking. More importantly, the timeline is long: first deployment isn't until the second half of 2027, and volume production is targeted for 2028, nearly two years out. Whether additional named customers surface before then, or whether the story goes quiet through the rest of 2026, will decide if today's 18% jump was justified.

jukan-globalwafers-wafer-shortage-novara:
Taiwan's GlobalWafers confirmed at its Q2 earnings call on August 4
that a silicon wafer shortage has already begun.

All of its 12-inch, 8-inch, and 6-inch production lines are effectively
running at maximum utilization, and supply constraints have emerged
for some advanced 12-inch products.

@@REF@@GlobalWafers Warns of Emerging 12-Inch Wafer Supply Constraints (The Elec, 2026-08-06)|https://www.thelec.net/news/articleView.html?idxno=12856|https://cdn.thelec.net/news/photo/202608/12856_12958_1631.jpg

## Why Three Countries' Wafer Makers Are Saying the Same Thing

This shortage comes from AI chips, HBM (high-bandwidth memory),
silicon photonics, and advanced packaging all pulling on capacity at once.

Before any chip can be made, it needs a thin silicon disc to be etched on,
the wafer itself. That base material is what's running short.

Germany's Siltronic said at its July 30 earnings call that customer
inventories have normalized and safety-stock rebuilding has begun.

Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemical reported on July 24 that 300mm wafer shipments
grew at double-digit rates both year over year and quarter over quarter.

South Korea's SK Siltron is reportedly bringing new equipment online in
stages, but order growth is outrunning the pace of that capacity addition.

Three competing companies from three different countries saying the same
thing in the same quarter is what turns this into a structural signal,
not a coincidence.

## Why Contract Lengths Are Stretching From 3 Years to 8

The nature of long-term supply agreements (LTAs) between wafer makers
and their customers is changing.

Where these contracts once existed to lock in stable volume, they now
function more like customers securing capacity ahead of a shortage.

Contract lengths have stretched from around three years to five to eight.

Last month, GlobalWafers signed a 10-year supply agreement with memory
maker Micron, the longest in the wafer industry.

The deal includes prepayment-style financial support exceeding $500 million,
which greenlit Phase 2 of GlobalWafers' Texas plant expansion.

Shin-Etsu now supplies all of its 300mm wafers under long-term agreements,
and two-thirds of Siltronic's volume follows the same model.

@@TIME@@2026-07-20|Fire at Novara, Italy plant damages 8-inch back-end line|2026-07-24|Shin-Etsu reports double-digit growth in 300mm wafer shipments|2026-07-30|Siltronic reports customer inventory normalizing, safety-stock rebuild|2026-08-04|GlobalWafers Q2 earnings call confirms supply shortage underway@@Four companies signaled the same direction within the same three weeks.@@Company earnings releases and filings (Jul-Aug 2026)

## The Hole the August 4 Numbers Don't Show

But there's a gap in this shortage story that the earnings numbers alone don't explain.

GlobalWafers' Q2 gross margin came in at 20.7%, down 5.5 percentage points
from a year earlier.

That's the combined effect of legacy low-priced contracts, ramp-up costs
at new facilities, and depreciation starting on the Texas plant.

If supply were genuinely this tight, pricing power should already be
shifting to the company. It hasn't clearly shown up in the profitability
numbers yet.

@@REF@@GlobalWafers Q2 Revenue Rises 8.8% QoQ to NT$15.2B, But Novara Fire Weighs on Q3 (BigGo Finance, 2026-08-04)|https://finance.biggo.com/news/TW_6488.TW_2026-08-04|https://img.biggo.com/r9TiBDmBKzzU8izkOEM4gRmzulzVhHdAPwAsUkhrzgM/fit/1200/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2Vhcm5pbmdzX2NhcmQvMjAyNi0wOC9UV182NDg4LlRXXzIwMjYtMDgtMDRfMTc4NTk5Njg5MC53ZWJw.jpg

There's one more variable. A July 20 fire at the Novara, Italy plant
damaged its 8-inch back-end processing line.

Epitaxial production, the process of coating a thin layer onto the wafer
surface, is expected to restart by mid-August, but the incident is
expected to disrupt Q3 output.

After the fire, the company lowered its full-year revenue guidance
to "flat to slightly higher" than last year.

So why would a company claiming shortage cut its own annual outlook?
The likelier read is that a one-off fire is masking, for one quarter,
the price gains the shortage should otherwise be producing.

If the shortage story holds, it points to a structural shift in pricing
power toward wafer suppliers like Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, Siltronic, SK Siltron,
and GlobalWafers. Wafer prices sit at the very bottom of the chip cost
structure, so a rise there ripples into every chip built on top of it.

But this quarter's numbers are clouded by a one-time event. The line to
watch is second-half spot pricing. GlobalWafers has guided that second-half
spot prices will come in higher than the first half.

If that guidance is confirmed with numbers at the Q3 earnings call in
November, the shortage story survived the noise of the fire. If it isn't,
the Novara fire will have meant nothing more than a quarter of clouded
results.
jukan-cxmt-refuses-apple-dram-discount:
Apple asked China's CXMT for a DRAM price cut and was refused. Apple has long been the side that shakes up negotiations with its buying power, but this time it was the supplier that held the line. CXMT quoted prices at or above what Samsung Electronics and SK hynix charge.

Apple had been negotiating with CXMT over mobile DRAM including LPDDR5X to ease manufacturing costs on its next iPhone and other devices, a familiar Apple playbook of dangling cheap Chinese parts to pressure incumbent suppliers. This time the playbook did not work.

## Why the Chinese supplier could afford to say no

CXMT could reject Apple's demand because Chinese giants like Huawei and Xiaomi had already locked up its DRAM output through long-term contracts, driven by their own push for supply-chain self-sufficiency under US sanctions. With captive Chinese demand already absorbing its capacity, CXMT had no reason to bend to Apple's dual demand of tougher quality checks and lower prices.

@@REF@@CXMT Says No Thank You to Apple's Demand For A Price Cut, as Huawei And Xiaomi Hand It Rare Leverage (WCCFTECH, 2026-08-05)|https://wccftech.com/cxmt-says-no-thank-you-to-apples-demand-for-a-price-cut-as-huawei-and-xiaomi-hand-it-rare-leverage-report/|https://cdn.wccftech.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Apple-and-CXMT.jpg

Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are the accidental winners here. With a Chinese buyer soaking up low-margin commodity DRAM, both Korean makers are freed from having to dump cheap volume and can devote more of their lines to high-value memory like HBM instead.

## The real reason CXMT does not need to discount

There is a deeper reason CXMT can hold firm. Blocked from EUV lithography by US export controls, CXMT relies on older DUV tools and multi-patterning to print the same circuits, a process that requires roughly 30% more wafer starts than EUV-equipped rivals to produce the same DRAM output.

@@REF@@Apple's CXMT Gambit Collapses: DUV Cost Gap Locks In Samsung's Pricing Power (Tech Times, 2026-08-05)|https://www.techtimes.com/articles/323140/20260805/apples-cxmt-gambit-collapses-duv-cost-gap-locks-samsungs-pricing-power.htm|https://d.techtimes.com/en/full/471456/changxin-memory-technologies.jpg

By process generation, CXMT is estimated to be five or six nodes behind Samsung and SK hynix. Its next-generation LPDDR6 targets 12.8 gigabits per second, short of the 14.4 Gbps SK hynix is aiming for. The equipment ceiling becomes a performance ceiling.

That structure flips the story. Today's elevated price is CXMT's manufacturing floor, not its ceiling, since any real discount would make its sales unprofitable. Playing price disruptor was never an option CXMT could actually choose.

## The hand Samsung and SK hynix hold for second-half talks

Apple has fewer alternative-supplier cards to play going forward. If CXMT will not budge, Apple's next negotiating partner is Samsung or SK hynix, and both now have room to push for firmer pricing in second-half long-term contracts. The open question is how long CXMT's wafer-cost burden can hold. Tighter US export controls would push CXMT's costs higher still, cementing Samsung and SK hynix's pricing power further; a breakthrough in China's domestic lithography tools could unsettle this balance again.
meru-korea-isa-productive-finance-domest:
In the tax revision unveiled on August 3, the Korean government created a new account called the productive finance ISA.
Tax on interest and dividends inside it disappears and the lifetime ceiling doubles from the existing ISA, but the only things it may hold are domestic assets.

@@REF@@South Korea plans tax breaks to revive economic growth (UPI, 2026-08-03)|https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/08/03/special-taxation-act-tax-reform/2161785809142/|https://cdnph.upi.com/sv/ph/og/i/2161785809142/2026/1/17858092557035/v1.5/South-Korea-plans-tax-breaks-to-revive-economic-growth.jpg

An ISA is a tax favoured account that holds deposits, stocks and funds together and trims the tax on what they earn.
The existing Korean ISA exempts only the first 2 million won of gains and takes 9.9 percent of the rest separately, while the new account leaves interest and dividends untaxed with no ceiling at all.

Young savers get one more thing.
Anyone aged 15 to 34 with total salary of 75 million won or less can deduct 10 percent of the year's contributions from income. Paying in comes back as a deduction at year end settlement.

The annual contribution limit is 20 million won, and the account runs in three year contracts up to ten years in total.

## Looking only at the size of the bowl

@@BAR@@Existing ISA lifetime cap|100m won|10000|Productive finance ISA cap|200m won|20000|Japan's new NISA lifetime cap|18m yen (about 163m won)|16300@@On size alone the new Korean account is the bigger one. What the picture does not say is what may go inside it.@@Ministry of Economy and Finance 2026 tax revision (2026-08-03), Japan FSA NISA framework, converted at 906 won per 100 yen (checked 2026-08-05)

## What it is allowed to hold

The new account is limited to domestic assets: Korean stocks, domestic equity funds, and vehicles such as the National Growth Fund.
Exchange traded funds that track US indexes drop out even when they are listed in Seoul.

The target of that clause is not hard to see.
Korean retail investors held $161.1 billion of overseas stocks as of the end of September 2025, and the retail share of the country's outbound equity investment, less than one in ten before 2020, is now more than one in three.
The idea is to turn the flow that had been filling tax favoured accounts with US index funds back toward the domestic market.

@@REF@@Korea offers tax breaks to curb overseas stock outflows (Korea Herald, 2025-12-24)|https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10642876|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2025/12/24/news-p.v1.20251224.c7ece11b937447eaafcfdba0cd307f0b_T1.jpg

Holding domestic assets only also means that when one country's market shakes, there is nothing inside the account to share the shock.
The saver takes the tax break and gives up the spread.

## What the 9.73 million existing accounts lose

The same revision reaches back into accounts that are already open.
At the end of June there were 9.73 million existing ISAs holding 73 trillion won.

First, unused contribution room can no longer be carried into the next year.
A saver who put in 5 million won this year could until now add the missing 15 million on top of the following year's room. The habit of catching up in a year when the bonus lands is closed off.

Second, a contract that could effectively be rolled forward indefinitely is now capped at five years.
The force of a tax favoured account comes from untaxed principal going straight back to work, and closing the account every five years shortens that runway.

@@CMP@@The government's account|Tax on interest and dividends is gone and the lifetime ceiling has doubled. With an income deduction for the young on top, the account got bigger.|Meru's reading|The assets it may hold are fenced into the domestic market, and existing accounts lost carryover and duration. The bowl grew while what goes in it shrank.

What splits the two readings of the same bill is whether you look at the size of the account or at the range of assets it is allowed to hold.

## Where the productive finance ISA meets the December Assembly

What exists today is a government proposal, and tax bills are normally settled in the regular National Assembly session in December.
Before deciding how to use the account, the thing to watch is not the size of the benefit but whether the domestic assets only clause survives intact.

If it passes as written, the practical answer is to run a tax favoured account for domestic assets next to an ordinary account for overseas indexes; if the Assembly opens the door to foreign assets, one account does the job.
Anyone already holding an ISA also has reason to weigh that this year is the last one with carryover in it.

NAND is the chip that keeps the photos on your phone and the files on your laptop from disappearing.
It is storage memory that holds its contents with the power off, and in a data centre it is packed into a box and plugged into a server.
That box is an SSD, and the enterprise version has its own name, eSSD.

That box is what Solidigm sells.

## What changed since Intel sold
Intel put this business up for sale when NAND was not making money.
Prices swung hard while the cost of building capacity kept climbing, so Intel chose to leave the business entirely.

The picture is now inverted.
AI servers need somewhere to keep the data their models read, and enterprise SSD contract prices rose roughly 80% in the first quarter of 2026 alone.

## The QLC fork
NAND types are separated by how many bits go into one storage cell.
TLC holds three bits, QLC holds four. The more bits per cell, the more capacity in the same area, and the less rewriting the cell survives.

QLC, the type Solidigm is pushing, sits at the far right.|PantheraLeo1359531 · CC0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cell_types_SLC-PLC_in_comparison_20211102.svg

What AI servers mostly do is read stored data over and over.
When the erase and rewrite count is low, QLC's weakness barely shows and only its advantage remains, which is more capacity for the same money.
TrendForce described SK hynix Group's first quarter as a division of labour, with Solidigm ramping QLC shipments while SK hynix itself expanded TLC.

Whether the listed market accepts a number set at the peak of a boom is a separate question.

This is the fork.

The cost of running a model like Claude splits into two parts.

The yen moved from 164 to the dollar to 156.9 in a matter of days.

Washington intervened by selling somebody else's currency rather than touching its own.

For anyone defending the exchange rate, this is the picture they wanted.
For anyone who borrowed yen to buy assets abroad, it is the day the profit and loss flipped.

## Why a rising yen pushes US stocks down

Borrowing yen cheaply in Japan, converting it into dollars and parking it in US Treasuries or equities is called a carry trade.
Pay 1 percent to borrow and earn 4 percent where the money sits, and 3 percentage points a year accrue while you do nothing.
If the yen is weaker when the loan comes due, the exchange rate hands over a second profit.

The catch is that this trade is usually run on five to ten times the trader's own money.

When the yen rises quickly, the sequence runs like this.
The carry position takes a mark to market loss first, and when the collateral falls short a demand for more margin arrives.
If fresh money is hard to find, the US stocks and bonds in the account get sold.
The proceeds have to be turned back into yen to repay the loan, so the bid for yen grows again.
The yen ticks up once more, another trader's stop is touched, and the same loop starts over from the top.

That is why an unwind does not arrive slowly over months but lands in a few days.

serenity-fcc-optical-ban-indium-paradox:
The US government is drafting a ban on imports of new Chinese optical transceivers. But the American companies this ban is meant to help cannot scale production without a raw material China controls.

The FCC is weighing a ban on new Chinese-made optical transceivers, the modules that link AI data-center servers, framed as a national-security measure and targeted for this year. In its sights are China's Zhongji Innolight, which holds 27% of the global market, and Eoptolink, whose revenue has more than doubled in a year. Together the two supply most of Nvidia's 800G module demand.

## The replacements Washington has in mind

The intended substitutes are Coherent and Lumentum, both American, both already established names in data-center optical links.

@@REF@@The FCC Mulls Banning China-Sourced Optical Transceivers, Threatening Innolight's 27% Market Share As Coherent And Lumentum Prepare To Pounce (WCCFTECH, 2026-08-05)|https://wccftech.com/the-fcc-mulls-banning-china-sourced-optical-transceivers-threatening-innolights-27-global-market-share-as-coherent-and-lumentum-prepare-to-pounce/|https://cdn.wccftech.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/China-US-AI-War-2-1920x1262.jpg

## But those replacements are stuck on a Chinese raw material too

The catch is that the high-speed lasers Coherent and Lumentum build depend on indium phosphide, a compound semiconductor with no viable substitute above 100 gigabits per lane. China controls roughly 70% of global refined indium, and it placed indium phosphide on its export-control list in February 2025.

@@REF@@FCC Transceiver Ban Would Cut 60% of AI Data Center Supply; Western Replacements Need Chinese Indium (Tech Times, 2026-08-05)|https://www.techtimes.com/articles/323104/20260805/fcc-transceiver-ban-would-cut-60-ai-data-center-supply-western-replacements-need-chinese-indium.htm|https://d.techtimes.com/en/full/471415/photograph-taken-january-24-2025-shows-fiber-optic.jpg

Since then, China's indium phosphide exports have fallen roughly 72% year over year, and 6-inch wafer prices have jumped from about $1,400 to roughly $5,000 apiece. AXT, the US materials supplier that feeds Coherent, has piled up more than $60 million in backlogged orders. Lumentum's CEO has said the shortage will get worse than the memory-chip crunch.

## Even if the ban passes, supply stays short

So the ban's real effect differs from how it looks on paper. Blocking Chinese supply seems to hand volume to American firms, but those firms cannot expand output without the raw material China controls. Current US 800G transceiver capacity runs around 100,000 units a month, a fraction of total demand. If China tightens indium exports further, even Coherent and Lumentum, the companies the ban is meant to protect, could fail to fill the gap. If the US secures domestic indium production or alternate sourcing first, the ban could work as intended. The question is which comes first: securing the material, or enforcing the ban.

## Why yields and stocks now move apart

A correlation is a single number between -1 and 1 that measures how closely two things move together.
At 1 they always move in the same direction, at -1 always in opposite directions, and at 0 they have nothing to do with each other.

For more than a decade before 2020 this number was positive.
Rising yields signalled a stronger economy, and a stronger economy meant companies earned more, so share prices rose alongside them.

That link has broken.

Today, when yields rise stocks give way, and when yields fall stocks hold up.
August 4 in New York looked exactly like that: the S&P 500 closed at a record 7,736.52 while the 10-year yield slipped to 4.6%.

## Breakeven inflation has not moved from 2.2%

The Kobeissi Letter names inflation uncertainty and fiscal concerns side by side as the cause.
The numbers we pulled ourselves say the two do not carry equal weight.

The nominal 10-year yield was 4.7% as of August 3.
It splits into two pieces: what the market expects prices to do, and what money itself costs once inflation is stripped out.
The first is called breakeven inflation, the second the real yield.
Breakeven inflation sat at 2.2% on August 4, close enough to the Fed's 2% target, while the real yield was 2.4%.
Price expectations are quiet; money itself has become expensive.
The two readings come from different days, so they do not add exactly to the nominal yield.

That is where equities learned to fear the bond market.

## The number Treasury published on August 3

On August 3 the Treasury said it expects to borrow $739 billion in privately held net marketable debt this quarter.
That is $68 billion more than it projected in May, and Treasury attributed the increase to lower projected net cash flows.
The fourth-quarter estimate is $628 billion.
